Closest precedents address complementary pieces: [NARM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.04725) combines the final GRU state with attention-pooled recurrent states; [HGN](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) learns feature-wise and item-wise gates, but has no recurrent backbone. The algebraic precedent is [Highway Networks](https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/highway-networks.html): coordinate-wise interpolation with coupled carry/transform gates. These establish architectural ancestry, not evidence that this exact bounded last-item/GRU fusion improves recommendation. HGN’s component ablations do not isolate learned coordinate-wise interpolation against tuned fixed-weight fusion.

Mathematically, writing p=P(e), f−h=g⊙(p−h), so ||f−h||₂≤0.2||p−h||₂—not 0.2||h||₂. Thus the gate cap alone does not guarantee a conservative intervention. For scalar g, the branch-contribution norm ratio is g||p||/((1−g)||h||): with g=0.1 and ||p||=10||h||, the projected-item contribution already exceeds the recurrent contribution. Coordinate-wise gates additionally depend on coordinate alignment. Even a small representation change can reverse near-tied candidate scores.

Suggested controls, rather than established results: compare h-only, tuned fixed scalar weights, a learned global scalar, an input-dependent scalar, and coordinate-wise gates, holding projection and normalization constant. Normalize both branches after projection; [LayerNorm](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450) supplies a relevant mechanism, though independent learned gains can restore scale imbalance. Compare identity projection initialization when dimensions match against variance-preserving initialization; identity does not ensure branch alignment. Initialize g=0.2σ(a) with zero gate weights and bias log(g₀/(0.2−g₀)) for a chosen small g₀. Measure branch norms, gated-contribution ratios, ||f−h||/||h||, and validation HR@10; gate values alone are insufficient.
